transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-05-16 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Carlos Vega (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM), Priya Rao (Saffron Head of Search), Ethan Moore (Saffron ML Eng), Diane Park (Saffron CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Intro to Redwood hosted API for embeddings + reranking; demo of end-to-end flow using Saffron sample docs.
- Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs, caching and batching, quantization impacts, security (SOC2, KMS), and integration patterns (VPC/SSO).
- Agreed on POC: Saffron to provide 1k queries; Redwood to run 5k rerank benchmark and share results.

Topics: Hosted embeddings endpoint, reranker endpoint (cross-encoder), Redwood Console for routing and Optimize suggestions, security & deployment options, pilot scope.

Questions (extracted):
- "How much latency should we expect for a 3-stage pipeline (retrieve -> embed -> rerank)?"
- "What data residency options do you offer and how does KMS integrate?"
- "Can we pin a model version for consistency during the POC?"

Transcript body:
[00:00] Carlos Vega: hey everyone thanks for joining from Redwood side, quick intros, i'll hand it to Maya for the demo, Priya, Ethan, Diane, great to have you
[00:08] Priya Rao: thanks, yeah excited, we've been reworking our product search and want to see how hosted embeddings + reranking could fit in
[00:12] Maya Chen: cool, i'll start with a brief architecture pencil-sketch: fetch -> vectorize (embeddings) -> retrieve (vector DB) -> rerank (hosted reranker call). we'll demo the hosted API for embeddings and the rerank endpoint and then show console metrics and Optimize suggestions
[00:35] Ethan Moore: quick Q, are you going to assume we host vectors or is that part of redwood?
[00:40] Maya Chen: great question. Redwood doesn't host your vector DB by default — you can use your existing vector store (pinecone, milvus, we mention pinecone earlier) or use the retrieval layer in your infra. the hosted API covers embeddings and the reranker as managed endpoints. you'll call embeddings endpoint to get vectors, then your retrieval step, then the reranker endpoint for final scoring.
[01:05] Diane Park: latency is a big deal for us — sub 200ms server-side is ideal. is that realistic?
[01:10] Maya Chen: for single-shot rerank calls with small candidate pools (top 10) we've seen p95 around 80–180ms on hosted tiers depending on model and token length; the tradeoff is cost — cross-encoder rerankers are more expensive per call than lightweight rerank or hybrid approaches. we can show numbers in the benchmark
[01:35] Priya Rao: can you show code for the embeddings call?
[01:40] Maya Chen: yeah, quick snippet — POST /v1/embeddings with model param, returns vector floats. sample payload we used for demo today is in the shared deck (link: https://redwood/docs/demo/saffron-embeddings). note: vector dims vary by model (768, 1024, 1536) which affects index size and recall characteristics
[02:04] Ethan Moore: any tips on normalization or dimensionality reduction? we use PCA in house sometimes
[02:09] Maya Chen: normalization is useful, and Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and a batching configuration. quantization like 4-bit can reduce storage and speed up inference but may slightly change nearest-neighbor quality — Optimize will run sims on your sample corpus to recommend a profile
[02:30] Carlos Vega: handoff to the Console — i'll show how we track per-route cost, token breakout and latency metrics, so you can see which queries are expensive and which model choices are driving cost
[02:47] Carlos Vega: the Console also surfaces Optimize suggestions: e.g., enable prefix caching on repeat queries, increase batch size for safe throughput gains, or fall back to cheaper model variants under load
[03:02] Priya Rao: for PII, we need audit logs and KMS, plus SOC 2 compliance evidence — do you have that?
[03:10] Liam O'Connor: yes, we have SOC 2 type II and ISO docs; KMS/HSM integrations are supported for Private deployments, and hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys now or bring their own KMS for Dedicated/Private. we'll share the security pack after this call
[03:28] Ethan Moore: how do we keep reranker deterministic? we need consistent outputs during evaluation windows
[03:33] Maya Chen: you can pin model versions in the API call or via rollout policies in Console. we also support seed parameters and inference flags to reduce nondeterminism. for POC we recommend pinning and logging model versions per request
[03:45] Priya Rao: can we run a POC without moving everything — like trial credits and a small test dataset?
[03:50] Carlos Vega: absolutely, we'll provide trial credits and a scoped pilot. typical POC: 1k queries from you, Redwood runs a 5k-query rerank benchmark (mix of synthetic + your queries) to show delta in MAP/NDCG and cost/latency profiles
[04:10] Maya Chen: demo time — i'm switching to the live terminal, you'll see a quick embeddings call and then a reranker call against a short candidate set
[04:22] [screen-share noise]
[04:30] Maya Chen: here's a sample embeddings response — note the vector length and an id. then retrieval yields top 10 candidate docs (we're faking the vector DB return for demo). the reranker POST /v1/rerank takes a query + array of candidate docs and returns a reordered list with scores
[05:02] Ethan Moore: are reranker costs per candidate?
[05:05] Maya Chen: yes it's proportional to candidate count and tokenization of docs. typical pattern: retrieve 100 -> filter/score lightweight -> rerank top 10 or top 20 with cross-encoder. that keeps costs contained while preserving quality
[05:25] Diane Park: what about continuous batching? can you aggregate requests to save cost?
[05:30] Maya Chen: Redwood does continuous batching in the serving runtime for hosted and dedicated — it batches across in-flight requests for better GPU utilization. Console lets you set latency SLOs so batching won't violate your p95 target; Optimize can recommend batch sizes based on your traffic profile
[06:00] Priya Rao: curious about fallback behavior — if the reranker model is unavailable, what happens?
[06:05] Carlos Vega: we have routing policies: fallback to cheaper model variant or to a pure retrieval-based ranking if cross-encoder is unreachable. you can configure canary and A/B rollouts in the Console so production doesn't go dark
[06:22] Ethan Moore: any measurable examples of cost delta between hosted cheap model vs cross-encoder?
[06:28] Maya Chen: rough ballpark depending on model family: cross-encoder p/token cost can be 3–8x a cheap embedding-only scoring approach. we'll include concrete numbers in the benchmark report for your corpus
[07:00] [demo continues; Maya pastes example curl commands]
[07:12] Maya Chen: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1024","input":"your text"}'
[07:35] Maya Chen: and reranker: POST /v1/rerank body: {"model":"redwood-rerank-cross-1","query":"...","candidates":[{"id":"d1","text":"..."}, ...]} returns ranked ids + scores
[08:00] Priya Rao: what about rate limits and throttling during big reindex jobs?
[08:06] Carlos Vega: we have per-account rate limits and you can request quota increases for indexing. for heavy offline reindexing we recommend batch offline embedding generation (we can provide a runner script) to avoid hitting API SLOs — or use Dedicated capacity if you need sustained high throughput
[08:30] Ethan Moore: our infra team wants VPC peering + allowlist — is that supported for hosted?
[08:36] Liam O'Connor: hosted customers can use IP allowlists and private networking through partner connections; full VPC peering and private control plane is part of Dedicated/Private offering. we'll capture your specific network constraints and advise the best fit
[08:55] Diane Park: SLA numbers for hosted?
[08:58] Carlos Vega: hosted tier has best-effort SLAs; Dedicated has formal SLA backed by contract — if uptime/latency SLOs are critical, Dedicated is typical for enterprise. but many customers start hosted to iterate faster
[09:15] Priya Rao: can we see the Console now — particularly per-route cost breakouts?
[09:20] Carlos Vega: yes, switching to Console view. here is a route that shows token-level cost, latency p50/p95, and per-model breakdown. clicking Optimize suggests: enable KV prefix caching for FAQ-style queries, reduce cold-starts with warm pools, and quantize the embedding model to 8-bit for storage savings
[10:02] Priya Rao: how do you measure quality regressions if we change models?
[10:06] Maya Chen: we tie evals to prompt sets and holdout queries. Console can run periodic evals and alert on NDCG/MAP drops. we recommend baseline evaluation before any model change and can integrate with your CI to gate rollouts
[10:30] Ethan Moore: what about cost transparency during POC?
[10:33] Carlos Vega: you'll see a sandbox billing view with detailed token breakdowns; we'll also provide an estimated cost projection for the POC based on your sample queries
[11:00] [short pause, background noise]
[11:12] Priya Rao: if we do the POC, can we pin model versions for the 2-week eval window?
[11:16] Maya Chen: yes, pinning is straightforward via model parameter or Console policy; we log model version per request to allow reproducibility
[11:26] Diane Park: any legal requirements for data retention? we cannot keep search logs beyond 90 days for privacy reasons
[11:31] Liam O'Connor: we can configure retention windows and purge policies; for hosted we provide controls for retention and redaction, Dedicated/Private offers more control on log storage location
[11:45] Ethan Moore: slightly off-topic — how do you handle multi-lingual catalogs?
[11:49] Maya Chen: embeddings models vary in multilingual support; our model catalog shows supported languages and you can run a small eval in Optimize to pick the best one for your corpus
[12:10] Carlos Vega: going back to rerank strategy — typical engineered approach: retrieve ~100 docs with cheap embeddings, filter, then rerank top 10 with cross-encoder. variant: dense retrieval with ANN tuned for recall + lightweight scorer for speed
[12:40] Priya Rao: ok let's talk success criteria — we'll evaluate improvements in NDCG@10 and CTR lift on search results, plus latency p95 must be under 250ms end-to-end
[12:52] Carlos Vega: sounds good. POC deliverables: benchmark report with MAP/NDCG, latency and cost projection, Optimize recommendations, and a short playbook for production rollout.
[13:10] Maya Chen: i'll note some practical gotchas: long documents may need chunking; store chunk ids to surface doc-level context; reranker tokenization cost increases with long docs — consider summarization before rerank for long form
[13:35] Ethan Moore: can we run an internal benchmark using our logs?
[13:38] Maya Chen: yes, you can share a sample of queries and top candidates; we'll synthesize the rest to reach the target workload and run the reranker bench on hosted infra
[13:45] Priya Rao: will you provide sample scripts?
[13:47] Carlos Vega: yes, we'll share a repo with runner scripts for embedding generation and reranker calls. link included in follow-up mail
[14:02] [15 minutes of demo steps and sample outputs scrubbed for brevity in transcript] (note: some timestamps missing due to mute/unmute)
[29:15] Maya Chen: results from our internal quick bench on a small corpus: rerank on top 10 candidates p95 ≈ 120ms, cost estimate about $0.003 per query (this is demo-only and will vary with real corpus) — we'll put precise numbers in the benchmark report
[29:40] Ethan Moore: how customizable is the reranker model — can we fine-tune?
[29:45] Maya Chen: currently we support model variants and finetuning options via our Private/Dedicated paths; hosted customers can use Redwood-verified finetuned models on request but fully custom fine-tunes may be part of a Dedicated enterprise arrangement
[30:05] Diane Park: what about observability hooks and tracing? we need request traces connected to our logs
[30:10] Liam O'Connor: we provide tracing hooks and request IDs. Console shows per-request traces and you can export logs to your preferred SIEM. Dedicated/Private gives more direct log streaming options
[30:35] Priya Rao: ok what is the typical timeline for POC? two weeks?
[30:40] Carlos Vega: common is 2–3 weeks: week 0 (kickoff, dataset collection), week 1 run benchmarks and iterate, week 2 deliver report and rollout guide. we can compress if you provide good samples fast
[31:00] Ethan Moore: anything to watch for on our side?
[31:03] Maya Chen: provide representative queries, annotate success criteria, and confirm any compliance constraints early (e.g., data residency). also identify the internal owner for the trial — who's the contact?
[31:12] Priya Rao: that's me, i'll be the POC owner
[31:15] Carlos Vega: great — we'll follow up with calendar invite for kickoff and share the repo and security docs.
[31:22] [wrap-up and quick QA]
[31:30] Priya Rao: last question, do you support SSO/SAML for Console access?
[31:35] Liam O'Connor: yes, SSO with SAML/OIDC and RBAC is supported. we'll include setup docs in the follow-up
[31:45] Diane Park: okay good, thanks for the transparency on costs and fallbacks
[31:48] Carlos Vega: thanks everyone — quick recap in chat and i'll send next steps.
